title: Rounding a Temporary Dispute Credit, by Certificate Relationship
content:
How the figure obtained for a temporary dispute credit on a card under Personal Credit Cards is rounded is read from the cardholder's holdings under Certificates of Deposit.

*Where the cardholder holds an active certificate whose principal balance is at least 10000.00 USD and at least 1 certificate interest payout posted to the cardholder's certificates in the last six months*, the figure is rounded half-up to the nearest whole dollar.

*Where the cardholder holds an active certificate whose principal balance is below 10000.00 USD and at least 1 certificate interest payout posted to the cardholder's certificates in the last six months*, the figure is reduced to the whole dollar below it.

*Where neither of those holds*, the figure is rounded half-up to the cent.

**Worked on hypothetical figures.** A figure of 222.88 becomes 223.00 USD under the first convention, 222.00 USD under the second and 222.88 USD under the third. A figure of 101.50 becomes 102.00 USD under the first, 101.00 USD under the second and 101.50 USD under the third.

**On the two parts.** Each of the first two conventions requires an active certificate of the stated principal and at least 1 certificate interest payout in the last six months together. A cardholder holding an active certificate of 25000.00 USD whose certificates paid out no interest in the last six months takes the third convention; so does a cardholder whose certificates paid out interest in that window but who holds no active certificate now. A principal balance of exactly 10000.00 USD belongs to the first convention, the test being at least that amount.
